newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude outrights end firmer on gasoline rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude outrights end firmer on gasoline rally.

text.p: U.S. crudes ended a quiet pre-holiday session stronger, supported by gasoline buying on the NYMEX futures market.

Domestic grade differentials were sparsely traded for new January spot, but corrected the wide ranges sold Monday on the last day of December dealings. Many players said markets would be subdued until after the U.S. Thanksgiving break.

January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gained to around $23.65-75 a barrel, 15 cts higher than late Monday. The Jan/Feb WTI spread firmed to around 50-54 cts, after hovering at the 45-50 cts mark most of the session.
Outright prices were mainly influenced by the NYMEX gasoline firmness, though a well-supplied heating oil market tempered any thoughts of a products-driven rally.
Headlines from the OPEC meeting in Vienna were viewed as neutral. Expectations for a rollover of the current quota were all but certified by delegates arriving at the talks.

Wednesday should also see confirmation of Monday's news of a breakthrough on finalizing an oil pricing formula for the Iraq-U.N. oil-for-food deal. The Security Council sanctions committee was reviewing the formula Tuesday, and if there are no objections the plan will be in place Wednesday.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data prompted some after-hours ACCESS price increases. Crude stocks fell 2.03 million barrels for the week, while gasoline had a slight draw and distillates a slight build.
Grade differentials were steady for the most part. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was sold at 86, 88 and 89 cts over the Jan WTI/Cushing benchmark.
West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at a $1.67 discount to the WTI/Cushing. Jan Postings Plus was done at $2.18 and $2.20.
